name: ICCRN Amitriptyline
question: Does amitriptyline improve IC/BPS symptoms when added to education and behavioral modification in treatment-naïve adults?

arms.label: Amitriptyline plus education and behavioral modification
placebo plus education and behavioral modification

design.population: Adults with IC/BPS, bladder pain or discomfort and urinary frequency, symptoms for at least six weeks, and no prior significant IC/BPS treatment.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Foster 2010, Methods, Study design; Table 2; Results, paragraph 1

verdictNote: Primary intention-to-treat response difference did not reach significance; higher-dose subgroup was unplanned.
takeaway: In treatment-naïve IC/BPS, amitriptyline plus education and behavioral modification produced 12-week global symptom response in 74/135 (55%) versus 61/136 (45%) with placebo plus the same program; the primary comparison did not meet its prespecified significance threshold (P = 0.12).

reports.label: Primary 12-week report
reports.citation: Foster HE Jr, Hanno PM, Nickel JC, et al. "Effect of Amitriptyline on Symptoms in Treatment Naïve Patients With Interstitial Cystitis/Painful Bladder Syndrome." *J Urol.* 2010;183(5):1853-1858. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2009.12.106
reports.followUpLocator: Methods, Study Outcome Measures; Results, paragraph 1

results.measure: Moderate or marked symptom improvement at 12 weeks; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Intention-to-treat; missing primary outcomes counted as nonresponse; prespecified two-sided alpha 0.05.
results.locator: Results, paragraph 3; Table 3; Methods, Study Outcome Measures and Statistical analysis

results.endpoint: Global Response Assessment response with sustained high dose
results.measure: Moderate or marked improvement at 12 weeks among participants maintaining at least 50 mg/day; observed risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Unplanned, postrandomization subgroup defined by achieved and maintained dose; not a randomized comparison.

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12 weeks in 0–10 frequency score; mean difference
Mean change in voids per 24 hours from baseline to 12 weeks; mean difference

harms.label: Any adverse event
harms.note: All-cause adverse events; most events were mild or moderate.

harms.label: Constitutional symptoms, mainly fatigue or malaise
Gastrointestinal symptoms, mainly dry mouth or constipation
Neurologic symptoms, mainly dizziness or somnolence

delivery.label: Study-drug titration
delivery.value: 10 mg, then 25 mg, then 50 mg daily at weekly steps; 75 mg daily after three weeks if tolerated
delivery.note: Dose held at the highest tolerated level through week 12.

delivery.label: Maintained at least 50 mg/day through week 12
delivery.note: Equivalent assigned dose for matching placebo.
